summary: HF-026 still held at tests/rules/RuleCases.ps1:174-177 (Invoke-HarnessRaw), and it is now fixed. The path is read as the rest of the line with '(?m)^harness: scratch kept at (.+?)\s*$', and the folder is removed only when its leaf is fsa-rules-* and its parent is exactly [IO.Path]::GetTempPath() or $env:TEMP, the folder Python's tempfile uses. I wrote the test first, tests/bugs/SL-076-ScratchKeptPath.Tests.ps1. It takes RuleCases.ps1's own Invoke-HarnessRaw from its AST and runs it against a stand-in harness process that makes its scratch in %TEMP% the way Python picks it. It failed on the unfixed code for a spaced TEMP and for TEMP≠TMP, and on the real harness.py under the engine's python, then passed after the fix. I also ran RuleCases C-006 and C-014 for real with the engine, TEMP set to a path with a space and TMP set to a different folder. Afterwards no fsa-rules-* folder was left in either.

files.why: HF-026: Invoke-HarnessRaw now reads the whole 'scratch kept at' path, spaces included. It removes the folder only when the leaf is fsa-rules-* and the parent is GetTempPath (which reads TMP first) or $env:TEMP (which Python's tempfile.mkdtemp reads first).

The HF-026 test. It runs RuleCases.ps1's own Invoke-HarnessRaw, taken from its source, with its own TEMP and TMP. Shape Space: a spaced %TEMP%. Shape TempNotTmp: TMP≠TEMP. Shape Refused: the guard still leaves a folder outside TMP/TEMP, a folder whose leaf is not fsa-rules-*, and a nested fsa-rules-*. Shape Python (opt-in, needs -EnginePython): the real harness.py under the engine's interpreter.

tests.note: Written first, run on the unfixed RuleCases.ps1: 2 checks failed. Space: the folder '...\Users\John Smith\AppData\Local\Temp\fsa-rules-sl076' was not removed. TempNotTmp: '...\tmp-b\fsa-rules-sl076' was not removed, and GetTempPath returned tmp-a, confirming that .NET reads TMP first. Refused held.
The real harness.py, with an engine root that does not exist, exited 2 and kept its scratch in TEMP (with a space), not TMP. The scratch fsa-rules-j3_i63ji was left behind: 2 checks failed.

follow_ups: Python's tempfile.gettempdir checks TMPDIR before TEMP. A Windows shell that exports TMPDIR (some MSYS/Git Bash setups) would put the harness scratch in a folder that the fixed guard (GetTempPath or $env:TEMP, as HF-026 specified) does not accept, so it would still be left behind. Adding $env:TMPDIR to the accepted parents is a one-word change if it is ever wanted.

The C-006 fake engine and the new SL-076 Python shape show that RuleCases' own New-TempDir folders go under GetTempPath (TMP) while the harness scratch goes under TEMP. That is harmless now, but a later case that compares the two locations would need to know about it.
